subproblem.title: Besicovitch covering estimate: μ(A) ≤ C·t·ν(thickening(ρ₀, A)) when every x ∈ A carries a closed ball of radius in (0, ρ₀) with μ ≤ t·ν (parent steps 1–2)
subproblem.statement: For every N ∈ ℕ there is C ∈ ℕ (depending only on N) such that the following holds. Let μ and ν be measures on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, let A ⊆ ℝ^N be an arbitrary set, ρ₀ ∈ ℝ and t ∈ [0,∞]. Suppose every x ∈ A has some σ ∈ ℝ with 0 < σ < ρ₀ and μ(B_σ(x)) ≤ t·ν(B_σ(x)), where B_σ(x) = closedBall x σ. Then μ(A) ≤ C·t·ν(thickening(ρ₀, A)) in [0,∞]. Here μ(A) is the outer measure, and thickening(ρ₀, A) = {y : infEdist(y, A) < ofReal(ρ₀)} (Metric.thickening).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ (μ ν : Measure (Euclidean N)) (A : Set (Euclidean N)) (ρ₀ : ℝ) (t : ℝ≥0∞), (∀ x ∈ A, ∃ σ : ℝ, 0 < σ ∧ σ < ρ₀ ∧ μ (closedBall x σ) ≤ t * ν (closedBall x σ)) → μ A ≤ (C : ℝ≥0∞) * t * ν (thickening ρ₀ A)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the parent proof, i.e. the application of the Besicovitch Covering Lemma (Simon Ch. 1, 3.12) in the printed proof of estimate (1) of Simon 8.5.9, p. 219 ("By the Besicovitch Covering Lemma we then have μ_V(A_i) ≤ c j⁻¹ ‖δV_ℓ‖(W)"). The set E of parent step 2 is the arbitrary set A here, the single measure ν plays the role of ν_k, and the enlarged set is thickening(ρ₀, A). Statement and argument coincide with the accepted node root.density_semicontinuity-a1.besicovitch_ratio_cover-a1 (Submission.besicovitch_ratio_cover_estimate, commit b70dd9d5 on origin branch humanize-recursive/gmt-ch08/20261011t141839z-af4f31741f/root-density-semicontinuity-a1-besicovitch-ratio-cover-a1-a1), restated here under a fresh name (that node is accepted but not yet integrated, and its declaration is not present in this workspace).

Notation: B_σ(x) := closedBall x σ and B°_σ(x) := ball x σ. All quantities lie in [0,∞]. For an arbitrary set E ⊆ ℝ^N, μ(E) is the outer measure; Mathlib measures are monotone and countably subadditive on all sets. Closed balls are closed, hence Borel (measurableSet_closedBall), so ν is countably additive on countable pairwise disjoint families of closed balls.

1. Choice of C. ℝ^N = Euclidean N is a finite-dimensional real normed space, so it has the Besicovitch covering property (Mathlib instance Besicovitch.instHasBesicovitchCovering; Simon Ch. 1, 3.12). The class field HasBesicovitchCovering.no_satelliteConfig gives C ∈ ℕ and τ ∈ ℝ with 1 < τ such that there is no satellite configuration of C + 1 points with parameter τ: IsEmpty (Besicovitch.SatelliteConfig (Euclidean N) C τ). This C depends only on N. Fix it. Now let μ, ν, A, ρ₀ and t satisfy the hypothesis.

2. Radii. For each x ∈ A choose σ_x with 0 < σ_x < ρ₀ and μ(B_{σ_x}(x)) ≤ t·ν(B_{σ_x}(x)). Put B_x := B_{σ_x}(x).

3. Disjoint subfamilies. Index by the points of A, with centre x and radius σ_x for x ∈ A. Since 0 < σ_x and σ_x ≤ ρ₀, these data form a Besicovitch.BallPackage with common radius bound ρ₀. Apply Besicovitch.exist_disjoint_covering_families to it, using 1 < τ and the emptiness of satellite configurations from step 1. This gives sets s_1, …, s_C ⊆ A (indexed by Fin C) with two properties:
(i) for each l, the closed balls B_x, x ∈ s_l, are pairwise disjoint;
(ii) every centre lies in ⋃_l ⋃_{x∈s_l} B°_{σ_x}(x).
Every point of A is a centre, and B°_{σ_x}(x) ⊆ B_x (ball_subset_closedBall). Hence A ⊆ ⋃_l ⋃_{x∈s_l} B_x.

4. Countability. Each s_l is countable. Its balls B_x are pairwise disjoint by 3(i). Each B_x has nonempty interior: the interior contains the open ball B°_{σ_x}(x) (ball_subset_interior_closedBall), which contains x because σ_x > 0 (mem_ball_self). Euclidean N is a separable space, so Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_nonempty_interior applies.

5. The balls lie in the thickening. Let x ∈ A and y ∈ B_x. Then dist(y, x) ≤ σ_x < ρ₀, so y ∈ B°_{ρ₀}(x) (closedBall_subset_ball). Since x ∈ A, B°_{ρ₀}(x) ⊆ thickening(ρ₀, A) (Metric.ball_subset_thickening). Hence B_x ⊆ thickening(ρ₀, A) for every x ∈ A.

6. Estimate. In [0,∞],
μ(A) ≤ μ(⋃_l ⋃_{x∈s_l} B_x)
≤ Σ_{l=1}^{C} μ(⋃_{x∈s_l} B_x)
≤ Σ_l Σ_{x∈s_l} μ(B_x)
≤ Σ_l Σ_{x∈s_l} t·ν(B_x)
= Σ_l t·ν(⋃_{x∈s_l} B_x)
≤ Σ_l t·ν(thickening(ρ₀, A))
= C·t·ν(thickening(ρ₀, A)).
The steps are justified, in order, as follows:
- the first is step 3 and monotonicity of μ (measure_mono);
- the second is finite subadditivity of μ over l ∈ Fin C (measure_iUnion_fintype_le);
- the third is countable subadditivity of μ over the countable set s_l of step 4 (measure_biUnion_le);
- the fourth is the ball inequality of step 2, term by term (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum);
- the equality pulls t out of the sum (ENNReal.tsum_mul_left) and uses countable additivity of ν on the countable (step 4), pairwise disjoint (3(i)), measurable family of closed balls (measure_biUnion);
- the next inequality is step 5 with monotonicity of ν, multiplied by t;
- the last equality sums C equal terms.
This is the claim. If A = ∅ (which the hypothesis forces when ρ₀ ≤ 0, since then no σ with 0 < σ < ρ₀ exists), the claim is immediate from μ(∅) = 0, and the argument above also applies verbatim with every s_l empty. ∎

Formalization note (not a step of the argument): the accepted Lean proof of the identical type, Submission.besicovitch_ratio_cover_estimate in commit b70dd9d5 (`git show b70dd9d5 -- GMT/Ch08/Submission.lean`), follows steps 1–6 exactly and may be transplanted verbatim as the single theorem Submission.intcpt_vdb_besicovitch_cover_estimate. Do not declare the name Submission.besicovitch_ratio_cover_estimate in this subtree.
proof_key_steps: C and τ > 1 come from HasBesicovitchCovering.no_satelliteConfig for Euclidean N (instance Besicovitch.instHasBesicovitchCovering), so C depends only on N.
Choose σ_x ∈ (0, ρ₀) with μ(B_{σ_x}(x)) ≤ t·ν(B_{σ_x}(x)); these balls form a Besicovitch.BallPackage indexed by A with radius bound ρ₀.
Besicovitch.exist_disjoint_covering_families gives s_1, …, s_C ⊆ A, each with pairwise disjoint closed balls, whose balls cover A.
Each s_l is countable (pairwise disjoint sets with nonempty interior in a separable space), and every ball B_x lies in thickening(ρ₀, A).
Subadditivity of μ, the ball ratio bound, additivity of ν on the disjoint closed balls and monotonicity give μ(A) ≤ C·t·ν(thickening(ρ₀, A)).

subproblem.title: A.e. bound liminf_i ν_i(B_ρ(x)) ≤ c·μ(B_ρ(x)) on W for ρ < r, from a covering estimate with constant C and sup_i ν_i(thickening(r, W)) < ∞ (parent steps 3–6)
subproblem.statement: Let N, C ∈ ℕ, let μ and ν_i (i ∈ ℕ) be measures on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, let W ⊆ ℝ^N be an arbitrary set and r ∈ ℝ. Assume the covering estimate (H): for every set A ⊆ ℝ^N, every i ∈ ℕ and every t ∈ [0,∞], if every x ∈ A has some σ ∈ ℝ with 0 < σ < r and μ(B_σ(x)) ≤ t·ν_i(B_σ(x)), then μ(A) ≤ C·t·ν_i(thickening(r, A)). Assume also S := sup_i ν_i(thickening(r, W)) < ∞. Then for μ-almost every x (the exceptional set has outer μ-measure 0) the following holds: if x ∈ W, there is c ∈ ℕ with liminf_{i→∞} ν_i(B_ρ(x)) ≤ c·μ(B_ρ(x)) in [0,∞] for every ρ ∈ (0, r). Here B_ρ(x) = closedBall x ρ, μ of an arbitrary set is its outer measure, and thickening(r, E) = {y : infEdist(y, E) < ofReal(r)} (Metric.thickening).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N C : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (ν : ℕ → Measure (Euclidean N)) (W : Set (Euclidean N)) (r : ℝ), (∀ (A : Set (Euclidean N)) (i : ℕ) (t : ℝ≥0∞), (∀ x ∈ A, ∃ σ : ℝ, 0 < σ ∧ σ < r ∧ μ (closedBall x σ) ≤ t * ν i (closedBall x σ)) → μ A ≤ (C : ℝ≥0∞) * t * ν i (thickening r A)) → ⨆ i, ν i (thickening r W) ≠ ∞ → ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ W → ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < r → liminf (fun i ↦ ν i (closedBall x ρ)) atTop ≤ (c : ℝ≥0∞) * μ (closedBall x ρ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–6 of the parent proof, i.e. the remainder of the printed proof of estimate (1) of Simon 8.5.9, pp. 218–219. There the sets A_i = {x ∈ A : i_x ≤ i} increase to A and satisfy μ_V(A_i) ≤ c j⁻¹ ‖δV_ℓ‖(W) for ℓ ≥ i, hence μ_V(A_i) ≤ c j⁻¹ limsup_ℓ ‖δV_ℓ‖(W); so μ_V(A) ≤ c j⁻¹ for every j, and μ_V(A) = 0. The parent proof bounds instead by the larger, finite S = sup_ℓ ν_ℓ(thickening(r, W)). The Besicovitch estimate of parent step 2 enters only through hypothesis (H), together with monotonicity of the thickening in the set. The book's argument by contradiction is written directly as a proof that the exceptional set is μ-null.

Notation: B_ρ(x) := closedBall x ρ and S := sup_i ν_i(thickening(r, W)), with S ≠ ∞ by hypothesis. All quantities lie in [0,∞]. For an arbitrary set E ⊆ ℝ^N, μ(E) is the outer measure; Mathlib measures are monotone on all sets.

1. The exceptional set. Let P(x) be the statement "x ∈ W implies that there is c ∈ ℕ with liminf_i ν_i(B_ρ(x)) ≤ c·μ(B_ρ(x)) for every ρ with 0 < ρ < r". By definition (Mathlib ae_iff), "for μ-a.e. x, P(x)" means μ(E) = 0, where E := {x : not P(x)}. Since [0,∞] is linearly ordered, x ∈ E iff x ∈ W and for every c ∈ ℕ there is ρ with 0 < ρ < r and c·μ(B_ρ(x)) < liminf_i ν_i(B_ρ(x)). (If r ≤ 0 then E = ∅. The argument below covers this case too.)

2. Fix j ∈ ℕ and put a := j + 1 ∈ [0,∞], so a ≠ 0 and a ≠ ∞. For i ∈ ℕ let A_i := {x ∈ W : there is ρ with 0 < ρ < r and a·μ(B_ρ(x)) < ν_k(B_ρ(x)) for every k ≥ i}.
(a) The A_i increase. If i ≤ i′ then A_i ⊆ A_{i′}, because the same ρ works for every k ≥ i′ ≥ i.
(b) E ⊆ ⋃_i A_i. Let x ∈ E. Step 1 with c = j + 1 gives ρ with 0 < ρ < r and ((j + 1 : ℕ) : [0,∞])·μ(B_ρ(x)) < liminf_k ν_k(B_ρ(x)); moreover ((j + 1 : ℕ) : [0,∞]) = j + 1 = a (Nat.cast_add_one). In the complete linear order [0,∞], a value strictly below the liminf of a sequence along atTop is eventually strictly below the sequence (Filter.eventually_lt_of_lt_liminf; its boundedness side condition holds automatically). By Filter.eventually_atTop there is i with a·μ(B_ρ(x)) < ν_k(B_ρ(x)) for all k ≥ i. Since x ∈ W, x ∈ A_i.
(c) μ(A_i) ≤ C·a⁻¹·S for every i. Let x ∈ A_i, with ρ as in the definition of A_i. Taking k = i gives a·μ(B_ρ(x)) < ν_i(B_ρ(x)). Hence μ(B_ρ(x)) = a⁻¹·(a·μ(B_ρ(x))) ≤ a⁻¹·ν_i(B_ρ(x)). This uses a⁻¹·a = 1 (ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel, valid because a ≠ 0 and a ≠ ∞) and monotonicity of multiplication by a⁻¹. So every x ∈ A_i has σ := ρ with 0 < σ < r and μ(B_σ(x)) ≤ a⁻¹·ν_i(B_σ(x)). Hypothesis (H), applied with the set A_i, this i and t = a⁻¹, gives μ(A_i) ≤ C·a⁻¹·ν_i(thickening(r, A_i)). Since A_i ⊆ W, thickening(r, A_i) ⊆ thickening(r, W) (Metric.thickening_subset_of_subset; infEdist(y, ·) is antitone in the set). Hence ν_i(thickening(r, A_i)) ≤ ν_i(thickening(r, W)) ≤ sup_k ν_k(thickening(r, W)) = S (measure_mono, le_iSup). Multiplying by C·a⁻¹ gives μ(A_i) ≤ C·a⁻¹·S.
